GAP [1]: The mechanism by which USP7 causes KRAS stability is unknown AND understanding this relationship is crucial for developing effective strategies to counteract KRAS inhibitor resistance in NSCLC.

GAP [2]: No study has tested whether TBK1 interacts with KRAS under inflammatory conditions AND elucidating this interaction could provide insights into the early inflammatory adaptive phase and enhance responses to KRAS inhibition.

GAP [3]: It is unclear whether AcCoA acts upstream or downstream of NLRX1 in the mitophagy response AND characterizing this relationship could reveal new targets for modulating drug resistance.

GAP [4]: The causal path USP7 → KRAS → HRAS and RHEB is missing experimental validation of the HRAS intermediate AND understanding this relationship could provide a more complete picture of how KRAS inhibitor resistance arises in NSCLC.

GAP [5]: The mechanism by which AcCoA-NLRX1 axis causes drug resistance to KRAS G12C inhibitors is incomplete AND elucidating this relationship could reveal new targets for modulating drug efficacy and treatment response.
